questions.question: In which year did the 86th Constitutional Amendment add the 11 th Fundamental Duty in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in **2002**.
 
• It introduced the **11th Fundamental Duty** under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty states: **"It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years."**
 
• This amendment was made to align with the insertion of Article 21A, which made the Right to Education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The 86th Amendment emphasized the importance of education as a constitutional obligation for both the state and parents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Originally, the Indian Constitution did not have any provisions for Fundamental Duties.
 
• They were added by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Currently, there are **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51A of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (Article 21A)**
 
 
• Article 21A was introduced by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
 
• It makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The Right to Education Act (RTE), 2009, was enacted to give effect to this constitutional provision.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution," it introduced significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added the concept of Fundamental Duties and expanded the scope of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
 
 
• **Other Constitutional Amendments Related to Education**
 
 
• **93rd Amendment Act, 2005:** Introduced Article 15(5) to enable reservation in educational institutions for socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• **104th Amendment Act, 2019:** Extended reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in legislatures and educational institutions.

questions.question: Emani Sankara Sastry was one of the first Carnatic maestros to use a contact microphone to harness the full potential of which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Veena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Emani Sankara Sastry, a renowned Carnatic musician, is credited with pioneering the use of a contact microphone to amplify the sound of the **Veena**.
 
• He adapted and modernized the traditional playing style of the Veena, making it more suitable for larger audiences in concert settings.
 
• Sastry's innovation enhanced the tonal clarity and projection of the Veena, especially for live performances.
 
• His efforts contributed significantly to increasing the versatility and prominence of the Veena in Carnatic music.
 
• He is remembered as a master of the Veena and for his contributions to Carnatic music, including his innovative techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Veena:**

 
 
• The Veena is a traditional string instrument commonly used in Carnatic music, with a history dating back over 2,000 years.
 
• It typically consists of a large resonating body, a long fretted neck, and four main strings for melody, along with three drone strings.
 
• The Saraswati Veena is the most commonly played version in South Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Contact Microphone:**
 
 
• A contact microphone is designed to pick up vibrations directly from an object, rather than from the air.
 
• It is often used with acoustic instruments to amplify their sound without compromising tonal quality.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, originating in South India.
 
• It emphasizes vocal compositions and complex melodic structures known as ragas and rhythmic patterns called talas.
 
 
 
• **Emani Sankara Sastry’s Legacy:**
 
 
• He received several awards, including the prestigious Padma Shri, for his contributions to music.
 
• He trained many students who went on to become distinguished Veena artists.

questions.question: The Nile River, located in ______________, has long been recognised as the world's longest river extending 6,695 km.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North-Eastern Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nile River is located in **North-Eastern Africa**, flowing through countries such as Egypt, Sudan, and Uganda.
 
• It is widely recognized as the **world's longest river**, spanning approximately 6,695 kilometers (4,160 miles).
 
• The Nile has two major tributaries: the **White Nile**, originating from Lake Victoria, and the **Blue Nile**, originating from Lake Tana in Ethiopia.
 
• It flows northward and empties into the Mediterranean Sea, making it unique among major world rivers.
 
• The river has historically been crucial for **agriculture, transportation, and civilization** in the region, especially for ancient Egypt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance in Ancient Civilization:**

 
 
• The Nile River played a central role in the development of ancient Egyptian civilization, serving as a source of water, transportation, and fertile soil for agriculture.
 
• The annual flooding of the Nile provided nutrient-rich silt, which was essential for farming in the arid region.
 
 
 
• **Hydrology:**
 
 
• The Nile is fed by its two tributaries: the White Nile (longer but with less water flow) and the Blue Nile (shorter but contributes the majority of the water volume).
 
• The river basin covers approximately 3 million square kilometers across 11 countries, making it a critical water resource.
 
 
 
• **Modern Usage:**
 
 
• The Nile River supports millions of people through irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power.
 
• It remains a vital lifeline for agriculture and urban water supply in countries like Egypt and Sudan.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Challenges:**
 
 
• Climate change and upstream dam projects, such as Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam, have raised concerns over water distribution and ecological impacts.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to balance the needs of the countries sharing the Nile's resources through agreements and negotiations.

questions.question: Who among the following acts as the chairman of the Planning Commission of the state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Chief Minister** of a state acts as the chairman of the **State Planning Commission**.
 
• The State Planning Commission is responsible for **formulating state-specific development plans** in alignment with national goals.
 
• The Chief Minister holds the primary executive authority in the state and ensures coordination among various departments for implementing developmental schemes.
 
• State Planning Commissions were modeled after the erstwhile Planning Commission of India, which has now been replaced by the **NITI Aayog** at the central level.
 
• The Chief Minister’s role as chairman signifies the significance of their leadership in state development initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission of India**

 
 
• Established in 1950, the Planning Commission was responsible for India’s **five-year plans** and socio-economic development strategies.
 
• It was replaced in 2015 by the **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• NITI Aayog is a **policy think tank** of the Government of India that focuses on fostering cooperative federalism.
 
• It provides strategic and technical advice to both the central and state governments.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and is appointed by the Governor.
 
• They are responsible for the overall administration and development of the state.
 
 
 
• **State Planning Boards/Commissions**
 
 
• These are advisory bodies that assist in planning and implementing development initiatives at the state level.
 
• They work closely with the respective Chief Ministers and state departments.

questions.question: Which industry is considered a 'service industry'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tourism industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tourism industry is classified as a **service industry** because it provides intangible services such as hospitality, transportation, and entertainment to travelers.
 
• It contributes significantly to the economy by generating **employment opportunities** and revenue through both domestic and international tourism.
 
• Tourism involves services like travel arrangements, accommodation, food, and recreational activities, making it a key part of the **tertiary sector** of the economy.
 
• Globally, the tourism industry is one of the largest economic sectors, contributing around **10% of global GDP** (source: World Travel & Tourism Council, 2023).
 
• India, for instance, has a thriving tourism sector, contributing approximately **5.8% to its GDP** and employing millions in 2022 (source: Ministry of Tourism, India).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Service Industry:**

 
 
• It is part of the **tertiary sector** of an economy, focusing on providing services rather than goods.
 
• Examples include healthcare, education, financial services, and tourism.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Tourism:**
 
 
• Promotes regional development by boosting infrastructure such as roads, airports, and hospitality facilities.
 
• Encourages foreign exchange earnings through international tourist arrivals.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Tourism:**
 
 
• Focuses on minimizing environmental impact while supporting local economies and cultural heritage.
 
• Includes eco-tourism, cultural tourism, and community-based tourism initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Tourism in India:**
 
 
• India is known for its diverse attractions, including historical monuments, natural landscapes, and cultural festivals.
 
• Popular destinations include the Taj Mahal, Kerala backwaters, Rajasthan’s forts, and Himachal Pradesh's hill stations.

questions.question: A new cricket ball shall weigh not less than 155.9 g, nor more than _______ g, for standard conditions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**163**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A new cricket ball used in standard conditions must weigh **not less than 155.9 grams** and **not more than 163 grams** as per the **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) Laws of Cricket**.
 
• The weight limit for cricket balls is crucial to maintain fairness and uniformity in the game, ensuring no undue advantage for bowlers or batsmen.
 
• These specifications are outlined in Law 4 of the MCC Laws of Cricket, which governs the dimensions and weight of a cricket ball.
 
• The diameter of a cricket ball is also regulated and should measure between **22.4 cm and 22.9 cm**.
 
• The weight and size standards apply to Test matches, One-Day Internationals (ODIs), and T20 Internationals unless specified otherwise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)**

 
 
• The MCC is the **custodian of the Laws of Cricket** and was founded in 1787.
 
• It is based at Lord's Cricket Ground in London, often referred to as the "Home of Cricket."
 
• MCC is responsible for maintaining and updating the Laws of Cricket, ensuring consistency across all formats of the game.
 
 
 
• **Cricket Ball Construction**
 
 
• A cricket ball consists of a cork core wrapped in tightly wound string, encased in a leather cover.
 
• The leather is dyed red for Test matches and white for limited-overs formats.
 
• The seam, made of six rows of stitching, plays a significant role in swing and spin bowling.
 
 
 
• **Standard Ball Usage in Matches**
 
 
• The same ball is used for 80 overs in a Test match unless it is damaged or lost.
 
• In ODIs and T20Is, a new white ball is used at the start of each innings.
 
• White balls deteriorate faster than red balls due to their coating and are harder to maintain throughout the match.
 
 
 
• **Ball Tampering**
 
 
• Ball tampering refers to the illegal alteration of the ball's condition to gain an unfair advantage.
 
• Common methods include using foreign substances, scratching the surface, or lifting the seam.
 
• It is prohibited under the ICC Code of Conduct, and offenders face penalties including suspension.

questions.question: Which of the following neighbouring countries of India has a state religion as Islam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pakistan** has Islam as its official state religion, as enshrined in its Constitution.
 
• According to the Constitution of Pakistan (1973), **Article 2** declares Islam as the state religion of the country.
 
• Pakistan's population is predominantly Muslim, with over **96% of its citizens adhering to Islam**, predominantly Sunni Islam.
 
• The Constitution also provides that laws must be consistent with the Quran and Sunnah, making Pakistan an Islamic Republic.
 
• Pakistan was established in 1947 with the aim of creating a separate nation for Muslims in the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Religion**

 
 
• A state religion is a religious body or creed officially endorsed by the state.
 
• Countries with a state religion often incorporate religious principles into their legal and governance systems.
 
 
 
• **Islamic Republic**
 
 
• An Islamic Republic is a state under a republican government that is officially based on Islamic principles.
 
• Examples include Pakistan, Iran, and Mauritania.
 
 
 
• **Religious Diversity in South Asia**
 
 
• South Asia is home to diverse religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, Christianity, and Sikhism.
 
• Each neighboring country of India has a unique religious composition and state policies related to religion.
 
 
 
• **Other Neighboring Countries**
 
 
• **Sri Lanka:** The state religion is Buddhism, but other religions are also practiced freely.
 
• **Nepal:** Previously a Hindu kingdom, Nepal is now a secular state with no official religion.
 
• **Myanmar:** While Buddhism is dominant, there is no official state religion.

questions.question: According to a Buddhist text, how many oligarchic republics or kingdoms, called Mahajanapadas, ruled ancient India during the 6th to 4th centuries BCE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Buddhist and Jain texts, ancient India during the 6th to 4th centuries BCE was divided into **16 Mahajanapadas**, which were powerful oligarchic republics or kingdoms.
 
• The term **Mahajanapadas** translates to "great realms" or "great countries" and represents the primary political and territorial units of ancient India.
 
• Some prominent Mahajanapadas included **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti, Kuru, Panchala, and Gandhara**, among others.
 
• The Mahajanapadas were spread across various regions of the Indian subcontinent, from the northwestern parts (like Gandhara) to the eastern regions (like Anga and Magadha).
 
• The rise of Mahajanapadas marked the shift from tribal settlements to organized states with centralized governance and fortified cities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Sources:**

 
 
• The Mahajanapadas are extensively mentioned in Buddhist texts like the **Anguttara Nikaya** and Jain texts such as the **Bhagavati Sutra**.
 
• These texts provide insight into the political, economic, and social conditions of ancient India during this period.
 
 
 
• **Types of Governance:**
 
 
• Some Mahajanapadas, like Magadha, were monarchies led by kings.
 
• Others, such as Vaishali, were **republics** governed by an assembly of elected representatives.
 
 
 
• **Major Cities:**
 
 
• Each Mahajanapada had prominent cities serving as administrative centers, such as **Rajgir** in Magadha and **Kausambi** in Vatsa.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Mahajanapadas played a critical role in shaping ancient Indian civilization and laid the foundation for the rise of large empires like **Magadha** and later the Maurya Empire.
 
• They contributed to advancements in art, literature, religion, and urban planning.

questions.question: When was the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award won by Karnam Malleswari?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1994-95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Karnam Malleswari** was awarded the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in **1994-95**.
 
• She is an Indian weightlifter and the **first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal** (bronze in the 2000 Sydney Olympics).
 
• The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's **highest sporting honor**, awarded annually for outstanding performance in sports.
 
• Malleswari was honored for her exceptional achievements in weightlifting, including world championship victories.
 
• She became a role model for aspiring athletes and significantly contributed to the popularity of weightlifting in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**

 
 
• Established in 1991-92, it is named after the legendary Indian hockey player Major Dhyan Chand.
 
• The award includes a medal, a certificate, and a cash prize of Rs. 25 lakhs.
 
• It recognizes athletes for their extraordinary performance at international sports events.
 
 
 
• **Karnam Malleswari's Achievements:**
 
 
• She won the World Weightlifting Championships twice and multiple medals in Asian Games and Commonwealth Games.
 
• Her bronze medal at the 2000 Sydney Olympics was India's first Olympic medal in weightlifting.
 
• She was awarded the Padma Shri in 1999 for her contributions to Indian sports.
 
 
 
• **Indian Weightlifting:**
 
 
• Weightlifting is governed by the Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWF).
 
• India has produced several successful weightlifters, including Mirabai Chanu and Satish Sivalingam.
 
• Indian athletes have consistently performed well in regional and international competitions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Award:**
 
 
• The Khel Ratna Award motivates athletes to strive for excellence.
 
• It helps in promoting sports culture and raising awareness about lesser-known sports like weightlifting.
 
• Awardees often serve as inspirations for the younger generation of athletes.

questions.question: In which year did the New India Literacy Programme begin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2022-23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The New India Literacy Programme (NILP) was launched by the Government of India in the financial year **2022-23**.
 
• It aims to address the issue of adult illiteracy across the country and is focused on achieving the goal of functional literacy for non-literates aged 15 years and above.
 
• The programme is aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which emphasizes the importance of lifelong learning and equitable access to education.
 
• The NILP replaces the earlier scheme known as the **Saakshar Bharat Programme**, which concluded in 2017.
 
• The implementation of the NILP involves coordination between central and state governments, leveraging **technology-driven methods** and volunteerism to enhance reach and efficacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functional Literacy:**

 
 
• Functional literacy refers to the ability to read, write, and perform basic arithmetic tasks essential for everyday life.
 
• The NILP seeks to ensure that adult learners can effectively engage in social, economic, and cultural activities.
 
 
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**
 
 
• The NEP 2020 provides a framework for transforming India's education system, focusing on inclusivity and lifelong learning.
 
• Adult education and literacy initiatives under the NEP emphasize skill development and digital literacy.
 
 
 
• **Saakshar Bharat Programme:**
 
 
• Launched in 2009, Saakshar Bharat focused on promoting literacy in rural areas, particularly among women.
 
• It was concluded in 2017, paving the way for the New India Literacy Programme.
 
 
 
• **Volunteer-Based Implementation:**
 
 
• The NILP encourages community participation through volunteer-based teaching and learning models.
 
• Volunteers receive training and resources to aid in the delivery of literacy programmes.
 
 
 
• **Technology Integration:**
 
 
• The NILP leverages digital platforms and e-learning tools to enhance accessibility and engagement for learners.
 
• Mobile apps and online modules are being used to facilitate education for adult learners.

questions.question: Who among the following has been appointed as India’s new Ambassador to the United States of America in July 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinay Mohan Kwatra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vinay Mohan Kwatra**, a seasoned diplomat, was appointed as India’s Ambassador to the United States in July 2024.
 
• Prior to this appointment, Kwatra served as India's Foreign Secretary, a role he assumed in May 2022.
 
• Kwatra has extensive diplomatic experience, including postings in Nepal, France, and the Permanent Mission of India to the UN in Geneva.
 
• He has also held key positions in India’s Ministry of External Affairs, including Joint Secretary in charge of the Policy Planning and Research Division.
 
• Kwatra’s appointment as Ambassador to the United States is seen as a strategic move to strengthen India-US bilateral relations in areas such as trade, defense, and climate cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of an Ambassador:**

 
 
• An ambassador represents their home country in a foreign nation and serves as the highest-ranking diplomat in the host country.
 
• Ambassadors work to strengthen bilateral relations in areas such as trade, security, and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **India-US Relations:**
 
 
• India and the United States share a comprehensive global strategic partnership, focusing on defense, trade, technology, and climate change.
 
• Bilateral trade between India and the US reached over $120 billion in 2023.
 
• Defense cooperation includes agreements such as COMCASA and BECA, enhancing interoperability between the two nations.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Secretary Role:**
 
 
• The Foreign Secretary of India is the top diplomat in the Ministry of External Affairs, responsible for implementing foreign policy and advising the government on international matters.
 
• Vinay Mohan Kwatra served as Foreign Secretary before being appointed as Ambassador to the US.
 
 
 
• **India’s Diplomatic Missions:**
 
 
• India maintains diplomatic missions in over 190 countries, including embassies, consulates, and high commissions.
 
• The purpose of these missions is to foster international cooperation, protect Indian citizens abroad, and promote India's interests globally.

questions.question: Who led the Aligarh Movement to modernise education for Muslims in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Syed Ahmed Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Syed Ahmed Khan was the founder of the Aligarh Movement, which aimed to modernize education for Muslims in India by promoting Western education alongside Islamic principles.
 
• He established the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College in Aligarh in 1875, which later became the renowned Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in 1920.
 
• The movement emphasized the importance of English language and modern sciences to bridge the gap between the Muslim community and Western advancements.
 
• Syed Ahmed Khan believed that education was essential for uplifting the socio-economic conditions of Muslims, who had faced setbacks after the Revolt of 1857.
 
• The Aligarh Movement played a pivotal role in fostering a sense of unity and intellectual growth among Indian Muslims during British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College:**

 
 
• Founded in 1875 by Syed Ahmed Khan, the MAO College aimed to integrate modern education with Islamic values.
 
• The college served as a model institution for educational reform and became a hub for intellectual and cultural development.
 
• It later evolved into Aligarh Muslim University, one of the premier institutions in India.
 
 
 
• **The Revolt of 1857 and its impact on Muslims:**
 
 
• Muslims faced significant socio-political and economic decline following the failed Revolt of 1857 against British rule.
 
• Syed Ahmed Khan sought to rebuild the community through education and modernization to combat the stigma and repression faced by Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Western Education:**
 
 
• Syed Ahmed Khan advocated for the adoption of Western scientific knowledge and practices to help Muslims compete in modern society.
 
• He believed this approach would foster progressive thinking and create opportunities for Muslims in government and administration.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Aligarh Movement:**
 
 
• The movement laid the foundation for Muslim nationalism in India and inspired future leaders like Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
 
• It contributed significantly to the socio-political awakening of Indian Muslims during colonial rule.
 
• Aligarh Muslim University remains a symbol of the vision of Syed Ahmed Khan, promoting education and research globally.

questions.question: In 1828, Friedrich Wöhler published a paper describing the formation of urea by combining which acid and ammonium in vitro?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cyanic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1828, Friedrich Wöhler synthesized **urea** for the first time by heating ammonium cyanate.
 
• The reaction involved the use of **cyanic acid** and ammonium to create ammonium cyanate, which then rearranged into urea.
 
• This discovery marked the first artificial synthesis of an organic compound from inorganic materials, **challenging the vitalism theory** that organic compounds could only be produced by living organisms.
 
• Friedrich Wöhler's experiment is considered a foundational moment in the field of organic chemistry.
 
• The reaction demonstrated that chemical processes in living organisms could be explained through physical and chemical laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urea (CO(NH₂)₂)**

 
 
• Urea is a nitrogen-containing compound that is a major end product of protein metabolism in humans and other mammals.
 
• It is widely used as a fertilizer and in industrial applications such as plastics, resins, and cosmetics.
 
 
 
• **Cyanic Acid (HOCN)**
 
 
• Cyanic acid is a simple, unstable organic acid that plays a key role in the synthesis of urea through ammonium cyanate.
 
• It is an isomer of isocyanic acid (HNCO).
 
 
 
• **Vitalism Theory**
 
 
• Vitalism was a scientific theory that posited that organic compounds could only be synthesized by living organisms due to a "vital force."
 
• Wöhler’s urea synthesis disproved this theory, demonstrating that organic compounds could be created artificially.
 
 
 
• **Friedrich Wöhler**
 
 
• Friedrich Wöhler (1800–1882) was a German chemist renowned for his pioneering contributions to organic and inorganic chemistry.
 
• His urea synthesis is celebrated as one of the most important milestones in the history of chemistry.

questions.question: In which of the following places are Reh and Boori Boot predominantly celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Reh Festival** is a significant cultural celebration of the Idu Mishmi community in Arunachal Pradesh, showcasing their rich traditions and rituals.
 
• **Boori Boot Festival** is primarily celebrated by the Nyishi tribe in Arunachal Pradesh to mark the arrival of spring and express gratitude for a good harvest.
 
• The Reh Festival is deeply rooted in the animist beliefs of the Idu Mishmi tribe and involves rituals to appease spirits for well-being and prosperity.
 
• Boori Boot emphasizes communal harmony and includes rituals, cultural performances, and traditional feasting.
 
• Both festivals are integral to the cultural identity of Arunachal Pradesh and attract visitors interested in tribal heritage and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh:**

 
 
• Known as the "Land of the Dawn-lit Mountains," Arunachal Pradesh is the northeasternmost state of India.
 
• It is home to numerous tribes, including the Nyishi, Apatani, Adi, Idu Mishmi, and Monpa, each with distinct cultural practices.
 
• The state is renowned for its biodiversity and scenic landscapes, including snow-capped mountains, lush valleys, and rivers.
 
 
 
• **Nyishi Tribe:**
 
 
• The Nyishi are the largest ethnic group in Arunachal Pradesh and primarily inhabit the central and western parts of the state.
 
• They follow animist traditions and worship deities associated with nature.
 
• Boori Boot Festival is one of their major annual celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Idu Mishmi Tribe:**
 
 
• The Idu Mishmi tribe resides mainly in the Dibang Valley district of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The Reh Festival is significant for this tribe and reflects their animist religious practices.
 
• The tribe is known for their craftsmanship, especially weaving intricate patterns in textiles.
 
 
 
• **Festivals in Arunachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Other notable festivals in Arunachal Pradesh include Solung, Losar, and Siang River Festival.
 
• These festivals are celebrated to honor nature, the agricultural cycle, and communal harmony.
 
• They play a vital role in preserving the state's cultural heritage.

questions.question: The temperature at which an oil starts to burn, leading to a burnt flavour in the foods being prepared is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**smoke point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The smoke point is the temperature at which an oil or fat begins to visibly smoke and break down, producing a burnt flavor and potentially harmful compounds.
 
• It is an important factor in cooking and frying, as heating an oil beyond its smoke point can negatively affect the taste and safety of the food.
 
• The smoke point varies depending on the type of oil or fat. For instance, refined oils generally have higher smoke points than unrefined oils.
 
• Common cooking oils and their approximate smoke points: Canola oil (~400°F/204°C), Olive oil (~375°F/190°C), and Avocado oil (~520°F/271°C).
 
• Oils with higher smoke points are suitable for high-temperature cooking methods like deep-frying, while oils with lower smoke points are better for dressings and low-heat cooking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boiling Point:** The temperature at which a liquid turns into vapor. Unlike the smoke point, the boiling point is not a relevant factor for cooking oils.
 
• **Ignition Temperature:** The minimum temperature at which a substance catches fire without an external flame or spark. This is much higher than the smoke point.
 
• **Critical Temperature:** The temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied, regardless of pressure. This term is not related to cooking oils.
 
• **Refined vs. Unrefined Oils:** Refining removes impurities, increasing the smoke point of oils. For example, refined coconut oil has a smoke point of ~450°F, while unrefined coconut oil smokes at ~350°F.
 
• **Health Implications:** Overheating oils beyond their smoke point can degrade nutrients and produce harmful compounds like acrolein, which is linked to respiratory and health issues.

questions.question: Dr. PC Mahalnobis is also known as _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Father of Indian Statistics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, an Indian statistician, is widely regarded as the **Father of Indian Statistics**.
 
• He is best known for introducing the **Mahalanobis Distance**, a statistical measure used in multivariate data analysis.
 
• Dr. Mahalanobis founded the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)** in 1931, which became a hub for statistical research and education.
 
• He played a pivotal role in India's economic planning, contributing significantly to the formulation of the **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956–61).
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan** in 1968 for his outstanding contributions to science and statistics in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahalanobis Distance:**

 
 
• It is a measure of the distance between a point and a distribution, used in multivariate statistics.
 
• This method helps in identifying and analyzing patterns in high-dimensional data.
 
 
 
• **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI):**
 
 
• Founded by Dr. Mahalanobis in Kolkata, ISI is a renowned institution for research and education in statistics and related fields.
 
• It conducts national-level exams for admission to its undergraduate and postgraduate programs.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• Dr. Mahalanobis was the chief architect of this plan, which focused on rapid industrialization in India.
 
• It emphasized the development of heavy industries and the public sector for economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Contributions to Science:**
 
 
• Dr. Mahalanobis introduced various statistical tools and methods that are still widely used in research.
 
• His work significantly influenced fields such as anthropology, economics, and meteorology.

questions.question: What is one primary objective of disinvestment in public sector enterprises?

options.text: To increase government control over industries
To generate revenue for the government
To reduce the efficiency of public enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To generate revenue for the government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Disinvestment** is the process of selling or liquidating government stakes in public sector enterprises to generate funds.
 
• The primary objective of disinvestment is to **generate revenue for the government** to reduce the fiscal deficit and fund developmental programs.
 
• It helps the government meet its **budgetary requirements** without increasing taxes or borrowing.
 
• Disinvestment in Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) is also aimed at **reducing the financial burden of loss-making entities** on the government.
 
• Proceeds from disinvestment are often used to invest in infrastructure, social welfare programs, or debt reduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic Disinvestment:**

 
 
• It involves selling a major portion of government shares in a PSE, along with the transfer of management control to private entities.
 
• Examples include the sale of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Air India.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**
 
 
• It is the difference between the total revenue and total expenditure of the government in a financial year.
 
• Disinvestment helps reduce the fiscal deficit by generating non-tax revenue.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs):**
 
 
• These are companies owned and operated by the government, either fully or partially.
 
• PSEs play a crucial role in nation-building by contributing to economic development and employment generation.
 
 
 
• **National Investment Fund (NIF):**
 
 
• A fund where disinvestment proceeds are deposited.
 
• It is used for capital investment in infrastructure and financing social sector programs.
 
 
 
• **Privatization vs Disinvestment:**
 
 
• Privatization refers to transferring ownership and control entirely to private entities.
 
• Disinvestment involves partial or full sale of government stakes, but ownership may or may not be transferred.

questions.question: The tribal dance, Kunbi, is predominantly performed in the Indian state of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kunbi dance is a traditional tribal dance form performed primarily by the **Kunbi community** of Goa.
 
• This dance reflects the **simple lifestyle and agricultural traditions** of the Kunbi tribe, who are among the earliest settlers in Goa.
 
• Kunbi dance is performed during festivals and social occasions, often accompanied by **folk songs and traditional Goan music**.
 
• The attire for the Kunbi dance includes **traditional red sarees** with unique draping styles, signifying the cultural identity of the community.
 
• It is considered an essential part of Goa's **folk heritage and tribal culture**, showcasing the harmonious relationship between nature and tribal life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goa's Tribal Communities:**

 
 
• Goa is home to several tribal communities, including the Kunbi, Gauda, and Velip tribes.
 
• The Kunbi tribe is one of the oldest and most prominent tribal groups in the region.
 
• Tribal communities in Goa maintain a close connection with nature and play a significant role in preserving the state's rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Other Traditional Dance Forms of Goa:**
 
 
• Besides Kunbi, Goa is known for other folk dances such as **Dekhni, Fugdi, and Mando**.
 
• These dances are performed during various festivals and cultural events, representing Goa's vibrant traditions.
 
 
 
• **Goa's Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Known for its beaches, Goa also has a rich cultural history influenced by tribal traditions and Portuguese heritage.
 
• The state's folk art, music, and dance play an integral role in its tourism and cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Tribal Heritage:**
 
 
• Efforts are being made to preserve tribal traditions through cultural festivals and tourism initiatives.
 
• Documentation and promotion of dances like Kunbi help in maintaining the identity of Goa's tribal communities.
